text: CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) from individuals with autoimmune diseases, including type 1 diabetes, are deficient in controlling autologous proinflammatory responses versus controls. Whether Treg dysfunction is causal or secondary remains unclear. Polymorphisms in Treg-associated genes such as IL2RA confer higher autoimmune risk, but the link between IL2RA polymorphisms and Treg function was unexamined. Using healthy subjects to avoid disease confounders, researchers showed that a type 1 diabetes-associated IL2RA haplotype correlates with diminished IL-2 responsiveness in antigen-experienced CD4+ T cells, measured by STAT5a phosphorylation. It is also associated with lower FOXP3 expression by Tregs and reduced ability to suppress proliferation of autologous effector T cells. These data suggest molecular and cellular mechanisms by which IL-2RA gene polymorphisms affect immune regulation and autoimmune/inflammatory disease susceptibility.
